messages:
alex: Kicking off a quick experiment plan for the embed/rerank endpoint. We want an apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic comparison that isolates kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache warm/cold behavior. Focus metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency spikes, and throughput (qps).

alex: High level: run small sweep on vector dims (512,768,1024), batch sizes (1,8,32), and payload sizes (128B, 2KB, 16KB). For each combo run: replay slice, synthetic poisson load with same inter-arrival, and a "cold" KV run (cache cleared) + warm run (preload keys to target hit rate).

maria: +1. I can export a 1h replay slice with real query length/profile. prefer not to run 24h by default.

sam: let's also lock quantization/profile and model hash so kernels are comparable. freeze: MODEL_HASH=sha256:abcd1234, QUANT=INT8.

jordan: Important: run with KERNEL_MODE=stable and KERNEL_MODE=auto to see selection differences. Also capture per-request kernel choice in traces.

alex: Example harness command i will use locally:
```bash
./rerank-harness \ 
  --mode=replay \ 
  --trace=prod_slice_2026-05-12_10-11.json \ 
  --kernel=auto \ 
  --batching=adaptive \ 
  --kv-warm-percent=50 \ 
  --vectors=768 \ 
  --batch-size=8 \ 
  --model-hash=sha256:abcd1234
```

maria: config note: for synthetic, use poisson lambda tuned to match p50 from replay so we compare tails not load. also seed the synthetic RNG.

sam: and add these instrumentation flags for consistency: 
```yaml
perf: true
trace_kernel_choice: true
collect_gpu_metrics: true
collect_kv_stats: true
```

perf-bot: run completed (quick summary): mode=replay vectors=768 batch=8 kv_warm=50 kernel=auto 
- qps: 420
- p50: 18ms
- p95: 86ms
- p99: 260ms
- p999: 920ms
- errors: 0.3% (timeouts)
- kernel_breakdown: aten_gemm=63%, fused_attention=37%

maria: p99=260ms looks high. do we have KV miss correlation? can we see p99 by kv_hit vs kv_miss buckets?

perf-bot: additional stats (kv buckets): kv_hit p99=120ms, kv_miss p99=480ms. cache hit rate observed=52%.

sam: that aligns with kernel fallback on misses; kernel selection log shows fallback to aten_gemm when seq_len>1024 or kv_miss happened that changed execution path. we should reproduce with a forced kernel toggle.

alex: ran a forced-stable (KERNEL_MODE=stable) run and got: qps=390, p95=92ms, p99=270ms. interestingly p999 still spikes ~900ms.

jordan: can we capture GPU occupancy and host stalls at those p999 points? probably CPU-side scheduling or tiny GC in Python repo.

alex: attaching a minimal repro for the p999 trace (copied snippet):
```text
[trace id=tc-195] request_id=xxk9 seq_len=512 kv_hit=false kernel=aten_gemm backend=cuBLAS time_total=912ms time_gpu=46ms time_host_wait=850ms
```

maria: host_wait=850ms is massive — likely queuing or mutex. check batching queue depth and slow caller threads. also validate that adaptive batching didn't grow batches beyond 32.

sam: quick kernel-bisect idea: run two builds (before/after change that touched kernel selection) and replay same trace. i have two commits to try: f4a9c2e -> d12b77a. can someone run a bisect harness?

alex: i'll queue that. also plan: produce a single CSV per run with fields: mode, vectors, batch, payload_size, kv_warm_pct, kernel_mode, qps, p50, p95, p99, p999, errors, kernel_breakdown. we'll store in gs://redwood-perf/rerank/2026-05-replay-vs-synth/

jordan: tiny nit: ensure payload encoding same (json vs msgpack) — that changes CPU preproc time.

maria: noted. I'll generate the 1h replay and synthetic seed later today and upload to the bucket. linking the trace when done: <gs://redwood-traces/prod_slice_2026-05-12_10-11.json> :link: 

perf-bot: scheduled batch of experiments: 18 runs queued (3 dims x 3 batches x 2 kv states). ETA ~ 6h on the perf fleet. will post CSV on completion. :rocket:

alex: thanks — next actions: 1) run bisect on commits sam listed, 2) perf-bot runs queued experiments, 3) collect flamegraphs for p99/p999 and inspect host wait sources. we'll reconvene tomorrow with the CSV and preliminary flamegraphs. :+1:

sam: if anyone sees an obvious regression in kernel selection code, ping me and i'll take the bisect.

jordan: also add a control run with batching disabled (batch_size=1 and batching=off) to separate batching vs kernel effects.

alex: done. i'll add that to the queued jobs. will update thread when CSV + artifacts are uploaded.

perf-bot: experiment batch complete. CSV: gs://redwood-perf/rerank/2026-05-replay-vs-synth/results_1859987654.csv. Flamegraphs: gs://redwood-perf/rerank/2026-05-replay-vs-synth/flamegraphs/

maria: grabbing the CSV now, will slice by kv_hit and send a quick visualization.

alex: awesome — thanks team.
